name: Health Systems and AI Vendors
title: Health Systems and AI Vendors
answer: Health systems are signing enterprise agreements with AI vendors for tools covered by business associate agreements. OpenAI's healthcare offering lists deployments at Boston Children's Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, HCA Healthcare and UCSF.

reading.body:
Health systems are buying enterprise AI under business associate agreements, and OpenAI's healthcare offering names Boston Children's Hospital, Cedars-Sinai, HCA Healthcare and UCSF as deployments.

The pattern is procurement, not piloting. These are large academic and national hospital systems signing enterprise agreements rather than running single-department trials, and the vendor is a general-purpose model provider rather than a clinical AI specialist. That matters because the contract, not the model, is where data use, retention and training terms get decided. A business associate agreement governs privacy exposure under HIPAA. It does not by itself determine whether patient data improves the vendor's models, which is a separate negotiation.

For AI scaling, the relevant constraint here is not compute or power. It is institutional trust and legal exposure. Hospitals are the buyers, and their willingness to sign depends on terms that no amount of data center capacity can supply. The four named systems are a small sample of American hospitals, and the data does not say what was deployed, at what scale, or with what results.

The data also does not cover cost, contract length, or whether these deployments replaced existing tools. One related paper audits health AI vendor claims in Nigeria and finds unverified performance and preventable harms, which is a reminder that named deployments are not evidence of clinical benefit.
